meta.scope: Indonesia Batch 3 — Commodity uniqueness (palm oil, nickel, coal/energy minerals) and first provincial / regional layer. Captures the resource-export core and the extreme spatial heterogeneity (Java vs outer islands).

candidates.title: Palm-oil production and estate-crop statistics
candidates.publisher: BPS – Statistics Indonesia / Ministry of Agriculture related
candidates.description: Statistics on crude palm oil (CPO) and palm-kernel production, area, and related estate-crop indicators. Indonesia is the world’s largest palm-oil producer; the commodity is central to exports, land use, rural employment and environmental debate.
referenced_by: Rural employment and regional GDP in producing provinces
candidates.notes: Highest-visibility agricultural-commodity node. Major uniqueness layer for Indonesia.

candidates.title: Nickel and downstream mineral statistics
candidates.publisher: BPS / Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources related / trade statistics
candidates.description: Production, export and downstream-processing indicators for nickel (ore, matte, battery-grade intermediates). Indonesia has become a dominant global supplier and is pursuing aggressive downstream industrialisation of the nickel value chain.
referenced_by: Provincial economic accounts in producing regions
candidates.notes: Strategic mineral node. Central to both export earnings and the government’s downstream industrial strategy.

candidates.title: Coal production and export statistics
candidates.publisher: BPS / Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources related
candidates.description: Statistics on coal production, domestic use and exports. Coal remains a major export commodity and a dominant source of domestic power generation.
candidates.notes: Major energy-commodity node linking the resource and energy clusters.

candidates.title: Mining and quarrying statistics (broader)
candidates.description: Broader mining and quarrying production and value statistics that contextualise nickel, coal, tin, copper, gold and other minerals within the national accounts and industrial structure.

candidates.title: Provincial GDP (PDRB – Produk Domestik Regional Bruto)
candidates.description: Official provincial gross regional domestic product series by industrial origin and expenditure. Primary quantitative measure of the extreme economic concentration on Java versus the resource-rich outer islands.
candidates.notes: Core spatial-economic node. Essential for the Java vs outer-islands contrast.

candidates.title: Java economic and demographic core
candidates.publisher: Derived from BPS provincial and national statistics
candidates.region: Java (DKI Jakarta, West Java, Central Java, DIY, East Java, Banten)
candidates.description: Relational node capturing Java’s dominant share of population, GDP, manufacturing and services. Forms the primary core against which outer-island resource economies are contrasted.
candidates.notes: High-level spatial core node for the archipelago.

candidates.title: Outer-islands resource and demographic periphery
candidates.region: Sumatra, Kalimantan, Sulawesi, Maluku, Papua, Nusa Tenggara, etc.
candidates.description: Relational node for the non-Java provinces that collectively hold the majority of land area and resource wealth (palm oil, coal, nickel, gas, etc.) but a minority of population and manufacturing. Captures the classic core–periphery structure of the Indonesian economy.
candidates.notes: Periphery counterpart to the Java core. Essential for later densification of specific resource provinces.

candidates.title: DKI Jakarta – capital special region
candidates.description: Capital special region. Highest provincial GDP per capita, dominant services and government functions, extreme population density, and the primary node of the national urban system.

candidates.title: Internal migration and urbanisation statistics
candidates.description: Lifetime and recent migration flows, rural–urban movement, and urbanisation rates derived from the Population Census and intercensal surveys. Documents the long-run redistribution of population (including movements out of Java and into resource and urban destinations).
referenced_by: Population Census and Long Form results
candidates.notes: Demographic-flow node that links the census to the spatial economic structure.

candidates.title: Downstreaming / hilirisasi industrial-policy statistics and framing
candidates.publisher: Derived from Ministry of Industry / ESDM / BPS trade and production data; recurring in official policy
candidates.description: Statistical and policy traces of the downstreaming (hilirisasi) strategy that bans or restricts raw mineral exports and promotes domestic processing (especially nickel). Continuously cited in industrial and trade policy.
referenced_by: Foreign-trade composition (shift from ore to intermediates)
candidates.notes: High-citation industrial-policy node unique to contemporary Indonesia.

candidates.title: Indonesia commodity and spatial-resource meta-node
candidates.publisher: Derived from BPS, ESDM and related sources
candidates.description: Meta-node that binds palm oil, nickel, coal, broader mining, PDRB, Java-core vs outer-islands contrast, and the hilirisasi policy frame into a coherent resource-and-space cluster. Captures the dual structure of a Java-centred industrial/service economy and an outer-island resource economy.
referenced_by: All commodity and provincial nodes in this batch
National accounts, trade and energy series
candidates.notes: Integrating node for the resource–spatial uniqueness of Indonesia.
